acceptance: Qualification covers C={1,2,4,8,16} for feasible profiles and C=32 for appropriate server-class systems.
Reports include throughput, latency percentiles, fairness, errors, locality, platform pressure, session-pool evidence, and separately attributable client CPU/memory.
A point that breaches preregistered client-headroom gates is labeled client-limited and cannot be selected as a headline.
A platform cannot publish a lower actual concurrency under a higher C label.
Recommended public points are supported by saturation and stability evidence, and the complete curve remains publishable.
context: Implements the proposed cross-benchmark score architecture. Preserve official TPC metrics as separate outputs. Numerical weights, size vectors, concurrency points, thresholds, and the M4 reference remain pilot hypotheses until methodology freeze.
description: Run the declared concurrency ladder against qualified dataset profiles. Identify saturation, instability, memory pressure, unfairness, and platform/session limitations; retain full curves and recommend display points instead of assuming S/C4, M/C8, and L/C16.
